topic: Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals (AI-901) certification exam preparation - refreshed 2026 edition built around Microsoft Foundry
exam_format: 40-60 questions, 45 minutes (65 minutes total seat time), passing score 700/1000, online proctored or test center. Question types include multiple choice, multiple select, drag-and-drop, and hot area. No prerequisites; certification does not expire. AI-901 replaced AI-900 on June 30, 2026 and awards the same Azure AI Fundamentals badge.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple select clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: Complete beginners to AI, business users, project managers, and technical professionals who want to validate foundational AI knowledge and hands-on familiarity with Microsoft Foundry. No programming experience required, though the Foundry SDK appears at an introductory level.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Identify AI concepts and responsibilities
domains.notes: Common AI workloads: computer vision, natural language processing, speech, document intelligence/information extraction, generative AI, and agents - matching workloads to business scenarios. Responsible AI principles: fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, accountability - and applying them to scenarios. How generative AI models work: LLMs and SLMs, tokens, embeddings, transformers at a conceptual level, choosing and configuring models, prompt/completion basics, common generative AI use cases and limitations (hallucination, grounding).

domains.name: Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry
domains.notes: The hands-on majority of the exam, in four blocks. (1) Generative AI apps and agents: write effective system and user prompts, deploy a model in the Foundry portal, build a lightweight chat client with the Foundry SDK, create and test a single-agent solution. (2) Text and speech: sentiment analysis, key phrase extraction, entity recognition, translation, speech-to-text and text-to-speech with Foundry Tools/Azure AI services. (3) Computer vision and image generation: image classification, object detection, OCR, facial detection concepts, image generation models. (4) Information extraction: Azure Content Understanding for extracting data from documents, forms, and unstructured content.

extra_guidance: This is a REFRESHED 2026 EDITION replacing a course whose students reported audio/visual sync problems and a mismatched chapter conclusion - production quality matters as much as content this time; every chapter script must have a conclusion that recaps THAT chapter's topics precisely. Marketing angle: 'rebuilt for AI-901 around Microsoft Foundry, with two full-length practice tests'. The two domain names and weights above are Microsoft's official skills-measured outline - use them verbatim. AI-901 is Foundry-first: where AI-900 asked candidates to describe Azure AI services, AI-901 asks how to BUILD with Microsoft Foundry (portal, Foundry Tools, Foundry SDK, Foundry Models including Azure OpenAI). Weight the course accordingly - roughly 40% concepts/responsible AI, 60% Foundry implementation. Explain every acronym; audience is non-technical. Labs: portal-based Foundry explorations (deploy a model, test in playground, try Content Understanding on a sample document), prompt-writing exercises, and matching-workload-to-scenario drills - all doable on a free/trial account without writing production code. SDK coverage stays at read-and-understand level (what the code does, not memorizing syntax). Include drag-and-drop and multiple-select question styles in practice tests. Cover classic traps: which workload fits a scenario (document intelligence vs OCR vs NLP), responsible AI principle identification, agent vs chat app distinction, Content Understanding vs older Form Recognizer framing. Final chapter must be a full exam simulation walkthrough with 45-minute time-management strategy.
